finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.trigger: Attacker can inject malicious SMTP commands in the email content.
finding.assumptions: The attacker can control the content of the email that is sent through the SMTP server.

finding.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
finding.trigger: If the email content is displayed in a web application without proper sanitization, it can lead to XSS.
finding.assumptions: The email content might be displayed in a web application.

finding.title: Improper Input Validation
finding.trigger: The password is read from a file without any validation, which could lead to issues if the file is compromised.
finding.assumptions: The 'secret' file might be accessible or writable by an attacker.

finding.title: Sensitive Data Exposure
finding.trigger: The password is read from a file and used directly in the SMTP connection without encryption.
finding.assumptions: The password might be stored in plain text in the 'secret' file.
